problem: Navigability of visually guided 3D game levels is hard to measure: prior navigation agents run in simplified simulators with engine state access, and prior affordance work only analyzes static screenshots as human-facing hints, never as the perception of an autonomous agent.
motivation: Designers steer players via landmarks, lighting and composition rather than explicit markers, especially in Souls-like ARPGs, yet there is no screen-only agent or protocol to test how far such visual cues can carry autonomous navigation in shipped games. A shared baseline and engine-free evaluation would enable both agent research and level-design analysis.
key_idea: Wrap a frozen single-frame STP/MSTP visual affordance detector with a finite-state pulse-based controller and an optional visual memory bank, and evaluate it in commercial ARPGs through a milestone-based template-matching protocol that needs no engine access.
insight: Correct per-frame affordance detection is not enough: failures come from tight geometry and collision, vertical structure, dataset bias (left-leaning STP preference at Irithyll M6), and salient-but-non-traversable decoys (Grand Archives M3). The FSM gives segment-level robustness (e.g. BMW RS 0→40%, DS3-GA RS 20→50%), but the memory bank only reweights existing candidates so it helps inconsistently (ER MS 38.3→52.0 but DS3-GA 88.3→78.3), indicating that long-range connectivity, topological maps or planning are required.
method: STP/MSTP perception (frozen): Faster R-CNN detects spatial transition points in a single RGB frame; a selector scores candidates with embeddings, global features, sector priors, temporal consistency and heuristics, and picks the argmax as MSTP.
Finite-state machine: states Scan, Align, Advance, Refine, RecoverLocal, EscapeStuck, LoopBreaker, driven by progress signals (MSTP box area change, SSIM between frames, median optical flow).

Pulse camera/forward control: normalized error of MSTP center to screen center yields proportional key-pulse counts (U/I/O/P camera keys, or mouse moves in Black Myth) with a Schmitt-trigger dead zone; W hold gated by heading alignment.

Visual memory bank: stores frame embedding, 64-bit pHash, chosen sector and GOOD/BAD/UNK outcome (by IoU stability of MSTP) with quarantine/active partitions and ANN retrieval; penalizes candidate sectors near past BAD decisions.

Milestone evaluation protocol: designer-chosen viewpoints captured as grayscale template groups via yaw sweeps; normalized cross-correlation detects hits; per-milestone time budget, and on timeout the agent reloads a milestone save to continue.
Agent variants: Naive (steer to MSTP with minimal recovery), FSM-only, Full (FSM + memory bank).

setting.backbone: Fixed pretrained STP/MSTP model (Faster R-CNN + ResNet-based selector) from prior work, plus hand-designed FSM controller and memory bank (no new training)
setting.training_data: No new training; perception model was trained by prior work on annotated screenshots from Dark Souls I/III (and other ARPGs)
setting.action_space: Discrete key pulses: 4 camera directions (U/I/O/P or mouse), forward W hold/release, no-op
setting.simulator: Real commercial games (Dark Souls I, Dark Souls III, Elden Ring, Black Myth: Wukong) on PC
setting.privileged: none at test time for the agent; milestone saves and template screenshots used for evaluation and repositioning after timeouts; enemies disabled

numbers_note: Custom pilot benchmark (RS = full-route success, MS = mean per-milestone success); no standard benchmarks. Baseline Naive variants omitted; per-milestone breakdown is in Table 3.
results: Screen-only agents traverse many segments (best MS 88.3% on DS3-GA, 83.3% on BMW) but full-route success is low (0–50%), and 0% on DS1-PW and ER. FSM beats the Naive baseline on most routes (BMW RS 0→40%), while the memory bank is inconsistent.
limitations: Tightly coupled to one pretrained affordance model with its biases; no alternative perception front-ends or baselines
Small pilot: six hand-picked routes, 10 runs each, no jumping or enemies, single milestone configuration and fixed time budget
No 3D/vertical reasoning, collision handling or long-range connectivity; memory can only reweight existing candidates
